note: Re-judged against RFC 4271 Section 5.1.7: "A BGP speaker that performs route aggregation MAY add the AGGREGATOR attribute, which SHALL contain its own AS number and IP address." On the RIB side, aggregateOwnAggregator and TestRFC4271RouteAggregationNextHopAtomicAndAggregator prove that aggregator=true emits speaker-own (65000, 198.51.100.1) — distinct from localIFv4 (198.51.100.10) and contributor AGGREGATORs — on BestChange.Attributes (length 8) and dispatched update-text commands, while aggregator=false omits AGGREGATOR and missing speaker local-as/router-id suppresses rather than forging a bogus AGGREGATOR. On the reactor wire side, planBatchAttrs (reactor_api_batch.go:1767-1795) handles both Builder-backed (batch.Attrs) and wire-backed `update text` (batch.Wire with APIContextID, srcASN4=true) aggregates, and TestRFC4271AggregateWireEncodingFor2Byte4ByteEBGPAndIPv6 verifies both subtests produce 8-byte AGGREGATOR toward 4-byte peers, 6-byte AGGREGATOR (no AS4_AGGREGATOR) toward 2-byte peers for 16-bit ASNs, and 6-byte AGGREGATOR (AS_TRANS) + 8-byte AS4_AGGREGATOR toward 2-byte peers for 32-bit ASNs > 65535. rib.go:1603,1711 also replays active aggregates to ordinary peers on peer-up. All three discrimination records in rfc/discrimination/rfc4271/RFC4271-5.1.7-1.json (RIB positive/negative on aggregateOwnAggregator, reactor positive on reactorAPIAdapter.planBatchAttrs) are current (producer-disable revert records).
upgrade_reason: Fixed planBatchAttrs (internal/component/bgp/reactor/reactor_api_batch.go:1782-1795) to transcode 8-byte wire-backed AttrAggregator in batch.Wire (srcASN4 && !facts.asn4) to 6-byte 2-octet AGGREGATOR (+ AS4_AGGREGATOR when ASN > 65535) for 2-byte peers, added wire-update-text (batch.Wire with APIContextID) and builder subtests in TestRFC4271AggregateWireEncodingFor2Byte4ByteEBGPAndIPv6 tagged for RFC4271-5.1.7-1 positive with a discrimination record targeting reactorAPIAdapter.planBatchAttrs, and fixed rib.go handleStructuredState/handleState to replay aggregates on peer-up for ordinary peers too.
